context: Interactive network adjacency matrix with reorderable rows/columns, community color encoding, and a side degree bar chart — a data visualization
first_impression: Deliberate and cohesive: the Tol Bright palette ties community colors across axis labels, bar chart, and legend into a single visual language, and the layout is confident with generous margins.
what_works: The Paul Tol Bright palette is a genuine design choice — colorblind-friendly, harmonious, and consistently applied across every encoding channel (labels, bars, legend swatches). The side degree bar chart with matching community colors is a smart addition that earns its space without cluttering the matrix.
what_doesnt: The 55°-rotated column labels at 10px monospace are borderline unreadable at the rendered cell size (~15px), undermining the 'does it work' check for the column axis. The default 'Name' ordering — the first view a user sees — reveals no structure and offers no visual argument; starting in 'Community' order would make the block cluster pattern immediately legible.
